name: Three-Act Structure
axiom: Something happens, it gets worse, it resolves; give each act its own question.
trigger: Pitch decks, keynotes, and proposals long enough that the audience needs to know where they are in the argument.

steps.text: Setup: the world and the question it cannot answer.
Inciting incident: the event that makes staying impossible.
Confrontation: obstacles escalate and alliances shift.
Midpoint: the protagonist stops reacting and starts choosing.
Crisis: the choice between two things they want.
Resolution: the world answers the opening question.

antiPattern.violation: Three equal acts, because the presenter divided the running time rather than the work, so the middle sags and the end rushes.
antiPattern.remediation: Give the confrontation the most room. Setup states a question; only the middle can make it expensive.
